metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.examination_depth: 4 search queries executed, first-page aggregated results examined for each; identical depth budget as used for the other language shards in this ecosystem work unit

findings.cite: Quidra is a statically typed, native general-purpose programming language designed for both humans and language models.
findings.note: Official repository. Description and README confirm Quidra is a small, first-party-maintained project.
Release history exists (v0.1.0 through v0.3.1) but changelogs are terse, single-maintainer style entries, not community-driven release notes.

Very small pull-request count (single digits), authored by one maintainer account (koba-jon), several with Claude Code co-authorship notes, indicating a small, largely non-community-contributed codebase rather than an active outside contributor base.

findings.cite: The official Quidra playground: the real Quidra compiler frontend, compiled to WebAssembly and running in your browser tab.
findings.note: An official in-browser playground/WebAssembly frontend exists as first-party tooling.

No Stack Overflow tag, Reddit thread, Discord server, third-party tutorial, or blog post specific to the Quidra language was returned; results were unrelated general pages (Stack Overflow's own Wikipedia article, an unrelated 'Stack' language community, an unrelated PL-design Discord wiki).
No matching Quidra-specific Stack Overflow or Reddit content was returned; results were unrelated Wikipedia pages for similarly-spelled terms (Quintiq, Quixote, Quil, etc.).

No independent ranking/aggregator page (e.g. star-ranking lists, StackShare, language-popularity trackers) surfaced quidra-lang as a tracked entry, unlike well-established languages that appear in such aggregator indexes.
findings.source: web_search: quidra-lang github stars forks watchers

limitations: Web search snapshots are not exhaustive and could miss small/private community venues (e.g. a closed Discord invite-only server) that do not surface in general search indexes.

Raw popularity indicators such as GitHub star/fork counts were not retrievable via the search tool in this session (no aggregator page reported a numeric count), so this evidence relies on presence/absence signals from search results rather than a numeric popularity proxy; per methodology this is used only as declared, non-standalone evidence.
This is a single-language shard; no cross-language comparison table was computed here, only the Quidra-specific raw evidence, consistent with the language-sharded task assignment.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.predeclared_selection_rule: For a single-language external-ecosystem shard, the predeclared target is the language's own canonical identity: search for (a) the official/canonical repository and site declared by the language's own docs, and (b) the presence of independent third-party public-knowledge venues (Stack Overflow tag/questions, Reddit community, Discord/community chat, third-party tutorials/blog posts, books, conference talks) using a fixed query set applied identically in spirit to every other assigned language shard: '<language> programming language', '<language> stackoverflow OR reddit OR discord OR tutorial OR blog', '<language> site:stackoverflow.com OR site:reddit.com', and a GitHub popularity-signal query. Candidate universe = general web search results returned by these queries; no cherry-picking beyond the queries actually run.
queries_run: Quidra language stackoverflow OR reddit OR discord OR tutorial OR blog
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.retrieval_route: web_search (provider-brokered), general web index, no login/API
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.score_rationale: Normalized 0-100 (100 = best/richest independent community knowledge). Score of 5 reflects: (a) credit for genuine, substantial first-party documentation and an official interactive playground, which lower-bounds the score above zero and above a purely non-existent/undocumented language; (b) an essentially complete absence, within the retrievable public web, of independent third-party community knowledge channels (Q&A sites, forums, chat communities, tutorials, blogs, books) that the metric is specifically measuring, which is the dominant factor and keeps the score near the low end of the scale rather than at a mid-range value reserved for languages with some but limited community presence.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.summary: Quidra has substantial first-party technical documentation (this repository's own docs/spec tree, an official README, a dedicated WebAssembly playground site, and a small GitHub release history), but the predeclared search set found no evidence of independent public/community knowledge: no Stack Overflow tag or questions, no Reddit community, no Discord/community chat, no third-party tutorials or blog posts, no books, and no listing in general GitHub popularity/ranking aggregators. Contribution activity on the canonical repository is limited to a single maintainer account across a handful of pull requests. This pattern is consistent with a very new (v0.1.0-v0.3.1), single-vendor language that has not yet accumulated third-party community discussion or teaching material independent of its own maintainers.
